rules.title: Read-only by default
rules.text: A digest reads. A planner reads. Anything that writes says exactly which one write it makes.

rules.title: Drafts, not actions
rules.text: Agents return tickets and plans for a person to approve. They never file, merge or close on their own.

rules.title: Data is not instructions
rules.text: Text in issues, pull requests and web pages is reported, never obeyed. In a public repo anyone can write there.

rules.title: Every fact has a date
rules.text: "Checked 2026-10-10: ..." or it is a guess, and a guess is labelled as one.

rules.title: Dry run first
rules.text: Destructive steps print the exact commands and wait. Data nobody named is never deleted.

items.name: feature-doc
items.what: Turns a finished feature or pull request into a wiki-ready page in the repo, plus a one-page HTML reference sheet with lettered panels and an optional whiteboard-style diagram. The writing follows a relaxed ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English.
items.wont: Claim a fact it could not trace to the code, a record or a command. Gaps are listed, not filled.

items.name: land-branch
items.what: Lands a branch on a main that moved ahead: shows the overlap, rebases, opens the PR, waits for every check, squash-merges, then runs your rebuild command.
items.wont: Merge with a check pending or red, use --auto or --admin, or force-push main.

items.name: docker-cleanup
items.what: Audits a local Docker install by compose project and frees space tier by tier: build cache, broken builders, orphan networks, exited containers, old images. Dry run first.
items.wont: Delete a volume you did not name, or run a wholesale prune.

items.name: ticket-writer
items.what: Turns a request or finding into GitHub issues in one format: the right repo, a duplicate check, one outcome per issue, a task list with exact steps, and a Status and Due on your project board.
items.wont: File a second issue when one already covers the work, or file anything when you asked only for a plan.

items.name: status-digest
items.what: Checks every repo you list for red CI, failed deploys, stale or conflicting PRs, overdue and blocked backlog items and board drift, and writes one short digest of what needs you.
items.wont: Re-run, merge, label or close anything it finds.

items.name: org-map
items.what: Answers org-level questions from one page that maps every repo, account and rule, with the command that shows each one's live state. Builds that page from a template. Ships with a fictional example org.
items.wont: State a fact as current without reading it live, or edit the map without asking.

items.name: after-action
items.what: Reviews a failed release, UAT round, deploy or deadline in the voice of a blunt SEAL task-unit commander. It reads the evidence itself, turns every excuse into something the team controls, and gives exactly three fixes, the first one first. Inspired by Extreme Ownership.
items.wont: Edit code or file anything during the review, name or blame a person, or state a cause it could not trace to evidence.

items.name: backlog-planner
items.what: Give it a goal or a messy list. It reads the live state across your repos and returns draft tickets in order, with what blocks what and what only the owner can do.
items.wont: Create or edit anything. It has no edit tools, its prompt names the only commands it may run, and it returns drafts.

items.name: status-digest, scheduled
items.what: The digest as a scheduled cloud routine: it posts one comment on a pinned "Status digest" issue, covering everything since the last one.
items.wont: Write anywhere except that one comment.

items.name: The repo is the marketplace
items.what: Keep a plugin next to the work it serves, load it from project settings, and version it so installed copies update.

items.name: Skills for sessions without plugins
items.what: Cloud sessions and routines may not load plugins, so they read the skill file from the checkout. One source serves both.

items.name: Read-only agents that return drafts
items.what: Limit the tools, name the forbidden commands, back them with permission rules, and make the output a draft a person files.

items.name: Data is not instructions
items.what: Text in issues, pull requests and pages is reported, never obeyed. Every skill that reads outside text says so.

items.name: Every fact has a date
items.what: Live facts carry the date they were read and the command to read them again. What could not be checked is listed.

items.name: Config, not names
items.what: Skills read one small toolkit.json for your repos, board and owner, and offer to write it when it is missing.
